newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - KEN DRYDEN NAMED PRESIDENT OF TORONTO MAPLE LEAFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - KEN DRYDEN NAMED PRESIDENT OF TORONTO MAPLE LEAFS.

text.p: Former goaltender Ken Dryden, who backstopped the Montreal Canadiens to six Stanley Cups in eight seasons, Friday was named president of the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Dryden, who played with the Canadiens from 1970-73 and from 1974-79, replaces Cliff Fletcher who was fired as president and general manager last Saturday. The Hall of Fame goalie, who also led Canada to victory over the Soviet Union in 1972, will hire a new general manager for the Leafs.

Dryden, a close friend of Maple Leaf Gardens director Brian Bellmore, retired as a player after winning the Stanley Cup in 1979, but has stayed in touch with the sport as a colour analyst during Olympic Games broadcasts and as an author.
The 49-year-old Dryden, an attorney who served as Ontario youth commissioner in the 1980s, has no experience running a hockey team.
He will try to turn around a franchise that has not won a Stanley Cup since 1967.
"Ken's mandate is clear, bring the Stanley Cup back to Toronto," said Maple Leafs owner Steve Stavro. "Ken Dryden knows hockey and he knows how to win."
Toronto finished in last place in the Central Division with a 30-44-8 record this season -- 23rd overall in the 26-team NHL.
